summary: Halyard template with counterparty edits that shorten return to 3 Business Days, delete backup retention, replace the data protection clauses with a statement that personal data will be shared, add an unlimited indemnity, and request Irish law and courts.

findings.quote: KILMACUD COMMERCIAL SYSTEMS LIMITED
findings.why: Counterparty entity details were filled in (Irish company, number 541892); a lawyer must confirm them against the company register.

findings.quote: Disclosing Party means the Party that discloses, or procures the disclosure of, Confidential Information to the other Party
findings.why: Disclosing and Receiving Party are defined so either Party can be either, and the obligations bind both equally.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: Definition is tied to disclosure in connection with the Purpose, covers marked or reasonably confidential information, and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, which is discussions about a potential commercial (distribution and resale) relationship between the Parties.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure of any software, prototypes or other tangible objects
findings.why: The reverse engineering prohibition is retained unchanged.

findings.quote: is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.why: All four carve-outs (public domain, already held, third party, independent development) are present with a 'written records or other reasonable evidence' standard.

findings.quote: may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives (including advisers, auditors, insurers) and Group members is permitted on a need-to-know basis with the Receiving Party liable for them.

findings.quote: to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: [[INS: three (3)]] Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: The return/destruction period is cut from ten to three Business Days, which is under the 5 Business Day minimum.
findings.draft_redline: 6.1 If requested in writing at any time by the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall, within ten Business Days of receipt of such request:
findings.note_to_counterparty: Three Business Days is too short for us to action reliably across teams and systems. We would like to restore ten Business Days, and could consider five if that helps.

findings.quote: Not used.
findings.why: Deleting 6.2 and 6.3 removes the exception for automated backups and legally required copies, and the rule that retained copies stay confidential.
findings.draft_redline: 6.2 Notwithstanding Clause 6.1, the Receiving Party and its Representatives may retain (a) copies of Confidential Information securely stored in routine, automated electronic backup or archiving systems which are not readily accessible in the ordinary course of business, and (b) such copies as are strictly required to be retained by applicable law, regulation, professional standards or the rules of any competent regulatory authority. 6.3 Any Confidential Information so retained shall remain subject to the confidentiality and non-use obligations in this Agreement for so long as it is retained, notwithstanding expiry or termination of this Agreement.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need to keep the backup and legally-required copy exception, as it protects both of us and retained copies stay confidential. We would like to reinstate clauses 6.2 and 6.3.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, and all intellectual property rights in or relating to it, shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted other than use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "as is" basis.
findings.why: Information is as is, no warranty, no reliance liability except fraud, and no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: Mutual publicity restriction requiring prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: shall include personal data (as defined in the Data Protection Legislation) relating to prospective end-users, customer contacts and key account personnel within the territory
findings.why: The edit states that end-user and customer personal data will be shared as Confidential Information, with no data protection terms or DPA commitment.
findings.draft_redline: 9.1 The Parties do not anticipate that the disclosure of Confidential Information for the Purpose will involve the sharing or processing of any personal data (as defined in the Data Protection Legislation), other than routine business contact details of the Parties' respective personnel involved in managing the discussions.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to share end-user or customer personal data under an NDA alone. If personal data needs to be exchanged, we would first need a separate data processing or data sharing agreement.

findings.quote: Not used.
findings.why: Deleting 9.2 removes the commitment to enter a separate DPA before any personal data is shared, while 9.1 says personal data will be shared.
findings.draft_redline: 9.2 If either Party identifies that it is necessary to disclose any other personal data to the other Party in connection with the Purpose, that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement that complies with the requirements of the Data Protection Legislation.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please note that a separate data processing or sharing agreement must be in place before any personal data is disclosed, so we would like to reinstate clause 9.2.

findings.quote: for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Two year term, 30 days' notice, three year survival and Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets, all as preferred.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Equitable relief is mutual and expressed as 'entitled to seek'; remedies are cumulative under 11.2.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party hereby covenants and undertakes to indemnify, keep indemnified and hold harmless the Disclosing Party and each member of its Group
findings.why: The inserted text adds an unlimited indemnity for any breach, and the playbook allows no indemnity, capped or uncapped, mutual or otherwise.
findings.draft_redline: 11.2 The rights and remedies provided under this Agreement are cumulative and do not exclude any rights or remedies provided by law.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not give indemnities in our NDAs and would prefer liability for breach to be left to the general law. We would like to remove the added indemnity wording from clause 11.2.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner
findings.why: Neither Party may assign without prior written consent.

findings.quote: our Board's preference is for this Agreement to be governed by the laws of Ireland and subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Irish courts in Clause 12.11
findings.why: The margin comment asks for Irish governing law and exclusive Irish jurisdiction, although the clause text still reads England and Wales.
findings.draft_redline: 12.10 governed by the law of England and Wales; 12.11 courts of England and Wales have non-exclusive jurisdiction (if a concession is needed).
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to move away from English law for our NDAs. We could offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction, so that either party may bring proceedings in Ireland if needed.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: The clause text keeps exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
